requirements.title: Intrinsic assignment finalizes the old variable between RHS evaluation and definition
requirements.source: 7.5.6.3, p1, p1.intrinsic-assignment-event, p1.unallocated-allocatable-exclusion, p1.after-expression-evaluation, p1.before-variable-definition, p1.allocated-variable-before-deallocation, p1.allocated-subobject-before-deallocation; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 103.
requirements.definition: Intrinsic assignment finalizes its variable unless that variable is an unallocated allocatable variable. Finalization follows RHS evaluation and precedes definition of the left side. If assignment would deallocate an allocated variable or allocated allocatable subobject, finalization precedes that deallocation.

requirements.title: Successful deallocation finalizes pointer targets and qualifying allocatable entities
requirements.definition: Deallocating a pointer finalizes its target. Deallocating an allocatable entity finalizes it except when it is the variable in intrinsic assignment, whose finalization is governed by p1. Pointer association, whole-allocation and argument/construct-association restrictions remain necessary.

pending.allocated-allocatable-entity: Pending a defined allocated record and successful STAT-checked deallocation, with a callback before the object is released.
pending.automatic-allocatable-scope-exit: Pending an unsaved allocated local leaving a procedure or BLOCK; this is the canonical automatic-deallocation path, not the nonallocatable direct-return rule.

requirements.title: A nonpointer function result finalizes after its innermost executable construct
requirements.source: 7.5.6.3, p5, p5.nonpointer-function-reference, p5.result-finalization, p5.after-innermost-executable-construct; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 103.
requirements.definition: A nonpointer function result referenced by an executable construct is finalized after execution of the innermost executable construct containing that reference. A function result is not an ordinary local finalized merely by returning from its function. Pointer function results and their targets must remain distinct.

requirements.title: Specification-expression function results finalize before execution begins
requirements.source: 7.5.6.3, p6, p6.specification-expression-reference, p6.function-result, p6.before-executable-constructs; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 103.
requirements.definition: A function result referenced in a specification expression of a scoping unit is finalized before the executable constructs of that scoping unit execute. The expression and specification-function purity/interface/order restrictions still apply; this is not permission to call an impure logging factory or to hide an impure finalizer behind a PURE function.

requirements.title: INTENT OUT finalization occurs in the invoked procedure before undefinition

requirements.definition: Invocation finalizes a nonpointer nonallocatable INTENT(OUT) dummy before it becomes undefined. That finalization is considered to occur within the invoked procedure. For an elemental procedure this means scalar or elemental final availability governs the invocation regardless of actual-argument rank.

accounting.rationale: Separates successful pointer-target/allocatable deallocation finalization from processor-dependent behavior on a deallocation error.

For the specified unreachable pointer-allocated object, both whether finalization happens and its timing are processor choices. There is no mandatory garbage collection, immediate callback or final-at-program-exit rule.
Complete advisory note connecting finalization-based storage management to defined assignment.

If deallocation has an error condition, whether finalization occurs is processor dependent. No fixed callback count, deliberate memory exhaustion, invalid pointer operation or arbitrary crash/status oracle is imposed. Any later observation must preserve this freedom and independently qualify safe error handling.
